grades: Students entering junior or senior year (high school sophomores and juniors during the application year)
name: CDC Museum Disease Detective Camp
org: CDC David J. Sencer Museum (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention)
city: Atlanta, GA (CDC headquarters, in person day camp)
what_you_do: This is a free day camp at CDC headquarters. It lasts five days. Campers work in teams. They act as disease detectives on public health topics. Examples are infectious disease, epidemiology and emergency preparedness.
who_can_apply: High school students in the summer before junior or senior year, at least 16 on the first day of camp (no exceptions). A government photo ID is needed for CDC security. Non-Atlanta residents may apply but must arrange housing and travel. Non-U.S. citizens may apply with the documents asked for.
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to attend. Campers cover their own housing and daily transportation.
duration: Five days, 8:45 AM to 4:00 PM. The 2026 sessions were June 22 to 26 and July 20 to 24.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The page says to check back in January 2027 for 2027 summer program information.
how_to_apply: The pages read do not describe the application steps. The camp page says the application is found through the FAQ page when it opens, and to check back in January 2027.
notes: Very competitive in past years, but numbers were not on the pages read. Sessions are fixed, campers cannot arrive late, leave early or miss days.
